artists.biography: Pure Reason Revolution is a British rock group formed at the University of Westminster in 2003. Their music incorporates elements of progressive rock and electronic. Members have a shared appreciation for the work of bands such as Pink Floyd, Porcupine Tree, Nirvana, Justice, Kraftwerk and Fleetwood Mac.

perplexity.description:
Coming Up To Consciousness is the sixth studio album by British progressive alternative rock band Pure Reason Revolution, released on September 6, 2024, via InsideOut Music. The album continues the band’s post-hiatus creative resurgence, following 2020’s Eupnea and 2022’s Above Cirrus. Musically, it blends atmospheric electronic textures with expansive rock arrangements, marked by dreamy moods, epic guitar riffs, and layered vocal harmonies. Drawing inspiration from artists like Talk Talk, Elliot Smith, The Smile, Arctic Monkeys, and Pink Floyd, the album features guest contributions from legendary session bassist Guy Pratt (Pink Floyd) and mixing by Bruce Soord (The Pineapple Thief), who also delivered the album’s first Dolby Atmos and 5.1 surround sound mixes.

Thematically, Coming Up To Consciousness is an intensely personal work, grappling with betrayal, deception, grief, mortality, and questions of sanity. The concise, eight-track structure—each song ranging from four to seven minutes—reflects a more focused approach compared to the band’s earlier, sprawling compositions. Lyrically, the album was shaped by recent life events, including the loss of frontman Jon Courtney’s longtime dog, which deepened the emotional resonance of the record. The addition of vocalist Annicke Shireen further enriches the band’s sound, marking a new chapter in their evolving lineup.

Critically, the album has been praised for its emotional depth and sonic ambition, with reviewers noting its balance of darkness and beauty, as well as its successful integration of electronic and rock elements. It stands as a significant entry in Pure Reason Revolution’s discography, reaffirming their status as leading figures in the modern progressive rock scene.
